definitions.explanation: Air taken into or expelled from the lungs.

examples.japanese: {息|いき}を{吐|は}いてください。
{冬|ふゆ}は{息|いき}が{白|しろ}くなる。
examples.english: In winter, your breath turns white.

examples.japanese: {深|ふか}く{息|いき}を{吸|す}いましょう。
{階段|かいだん}を{上|あ}がって{息|いき}が{荒|あら}くなった。
examples.english: I was breathing heavily after climbing the stairs.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}とは{息|いき}が{合|あ}う。
{息|いき}を{抜|ぬ}く{時間|じかん}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: I need time to take a breather.

examples.japanese: {走|はし}った{後|あと}で{息|いき}を{整|ととの}えた。
examples.english: I caught my breath after running.

notes:
{息|いき} refers to both the physical breath (air inhaled/exhaled) and the act of breathing. It appears in many idiomatic expressions related to effort, coordination, and relaxation.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {息|いき}を{吸|す}う: to inhale
- {息|いき}を{吐|は}く: to exhale
- {息|いき}を{止|と}める: to hold one's breath
- {息|いき}が{切|き}れる: to be out of breath
- {息|いき}が{荒|あら}い: to be breathing heavily
- {息|いき}を{整|ととの}える: to catch one's breath

IDIOMATIC EXPRESSIONS:
- {息|いき}が{合|あ}う: to be in sync, to work well together
- {息|いき}を{抜|ぬ}く: to take a breather, to relax
- {息|いき}を{飲|の}む: to gasp (in surprise or awe)

COMPOUNDS:
- {溜息|ためいき}: sigh
- {息子|むすこ}: son (different meaning — uses the kanji {息|むす} in a compound)
- {息切|いきぎ}れ: shortness of breath
